newsitem.title: UK: UK sets guidelines for open-ended investment firms.
newsitem.headline: UK sets guidelines for open-ended investment firms.

text.p: UK's panel on takeovers set guidelines on Thursday for open-ended investment companies, the regulations for which will come into force on January 6, 1997.
The panel said OEICs would be limited liability firms with variable capital. They would carry the right to vote in certain circumstances and may be listed on the stock exchange.

The panel said the City Code on takeovers and mergers and the rules governing substantial acquistions of shares (SARs) would not be applicable to OEICs as the share capital would be subject to continuous change.
"The Code and the SARs will be amended in due course to make it clear that they do not apply to OEICs", it said.
